title: Paramartha Guru Tale 86

full_text:
Another wandering fortune-teller arrived at the ashram, wearing rings on every finger, boasting that he could find hidden underground water, buried gold, and lost cattle through divine divination.

While eating lunch on the veranda, the astrologer removed a heavy brass ring set with a red glass stone and placed it on the windowsill.

When lunch ended, the ring was gone.

The astrologer turned upon the disciples: 'One of you has stolen my magical gemstone ring! Confess, or I will curse your ashram with barrenness!'

The Guru was distressed: 'No disciple of mine is a thief! But you are a diviner of hidden treasures; use your astrological arts to locate your ring!'

The astrologer drew circles in the dirt with a stick, muttered charms, and pointed to Matti: 'The planets reveal that the ring is hidden inside this disciple's waistcloth!'

Matti was stripped and searched: no ring was found.

The astrologer pointed to Peedan: 'It is inside his sandals!'

The sandals were shaken: no ring was found.

The astrologer pointed to the ashram well: 'It has been thrown into the deep water!'

Matti was preparing to dive into the cold well with a rope, when the ashram cat jumped down from the windowsill. Beneath the cat's tail, wedged between two books on the shelf, the brass ring gleamed in the sunlight!

The cat had merely pushed it behind a manuscript while chasing a moth!

Guru Paramartha picked up the ring and handed it to the astrologer:

'Here is your ring, O seer of the cosmos! It was on the windowsill where you left it! If your stars could not distinguish between a cat's tail and my disciple's waistcloth, your divination is as hollow as an empty coconut!'

The embarrassed astrologer pocketed his ring and hurried away without his lunch.
moral: A charlatan who claims to see the stars cannot locate his own ring under his nose.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Paramartha Guru Tale 86"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
